summary: WorldEntity generation-7 candidate #421 bounds persistent-state bytes and retained duplicate-diagnostic metadata, but canonical record metadata remains caller-sized: kind plus origin.worldId/regionId/generator/recipeKey use checkedNonEmpty() with no byte ceiling and the registry retains the owned record. A unique valid registration can therefore retain arbitrarily large metadata even when persistentState is tiny, so the new diagnostic-retention bound does not close the canonical-record memory envelope.
evidence: Inspected retained WorldEntity PR #421 exact head 863fd843b477d0b3761f31556183a641fbc6b7f3 after checking current main and the existing generation-4 through generation-7 lineage.
WorldEntity.isId() alone has an explicit 256-byte-ish Lua string length ceiling; checkedNonEmpty() only enforces string type, non-empty, and no control characters.

cloneOrigin() routes worldId, optional regionId, generator, and recipeKey through checkedNonEmpty(); ownRecord()/new() route kind through checkedNonEmpty(). None of those canonical retained metadata fields has a size or aggregate-byte fence.

createRegistry().register() stores the fully owned record in the closure-private records table for a unique id. PR #421 only sums entityId/kind/recipeKey bytes when deciding whether to retain a duplicate diagnostic; it intentionally does not bound or truncate the canonical record itself.

Search of open issues and current/retained WorldEntity PR lineage found no separate record-metadata byte-bound lane; existing #293/#378/#397 bound persistentState and #417/#421 bound duplicate-diagnostic retention, which is a distinct surface.
No Roblox Studio or engine evidence is implicated; this is a source-only retained-memory/domain-boundary finding.

metadata.recommendedNext: Have the active WorldEntity test-adversary/primary lineage add a bounded canonical-record metadata contract (prefer aggregate bytes over per-field arbitrary limits), reject over-budget metadata before registry retention, and prove exact-boundary acceptance plus registered fail-atomicity without truncating canonical truth.
